ticket-runner <version> init · <repo root>

Wrote:
  .gitignore: added `.worktrees/` and `.ticket-runner/`
  ticket-runner.json: created, with every setting left at its default
  docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md: written
  CLAUDE.md: created, pointing at docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md
  .claude/skills/ticket-runner/SKILL.md: written

GitHub:
  labels: created needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent
  merges: squash merging is on, and no other merge method was touched
  branches: switched on deleting a pull request's branch when it merges

Checked:
  ✓ `gh` is authenticated
  ✓ `claude` runs
  ✗ the `mattpocock-skills` plugin is not installed — an implement Stage has no skill without it
  ✓ a CI workflow is present in `.github/workflows`
  ✓ a Check is configured or inferable: npm test, npm run typecheck

Not ready: 1 item is yours to put right.

The first line names the Version doing the setting up (ADR-0007), in the shape
`run-summary.txt` describes, so a Target can be told which pipeline wrote the
files it is about to gain. Where a newer Version has been published, one line
follows it and nothing comes between them:

ticket-runner <version> init · <repo root>
A newer Version is out: 0.5.0, and this is 0.4.0 — upgrade with `npm install -g ticket-runner`.

Wrote:
  ...

It is the same line a Run prints, under the same conditions, and like a Run's it
refuses nothing: `init` sets the Target up either way.

Three groups, always in this order and always all three, however little each has
to say.

`Wrote:` has one line per file that changed, and `  nothing to write` when the
Target already had everything — which is what a second `init` prints. The
conventions document is the one file rewritten rather than left alone, and it
carries the Version that wrote it in a hidden marker on its first line, which is
read before its text is compared (ADR-0007). Five lines, one per case:

  docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md: written
  docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md: overwritten, because the copy here carried no Version
  docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md: overwritten, because the copy here was left by 0.3.0
  docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md: overwritten, because the copy here said something else
  docs/agents/pipeline-conventions.md: left alone, because 0.5.0 set this Target up and this is 0.4.0 — upgrade `ticket-runner` to rewrite it

The fourth is a copy marked with this very Version: nothing about the pipeline
moved, so whatever the difference is, the Target made it. Identical text is not
a line at all. A copy a newer pipeline wrote is the one this never touches:
rewriting it would take the Target backwards, so it is left and the upgrade is
named. None of the five is a `Checked:` item, so none of them changes the exit
code — a Target is not unready for carrying another Version's copy.

The Operator's skill is the pipeline's own text too, rewritten when it says
something else and left alone where a newer pipeline set the Target up, which
the conventions document's mark is how `init` knows. It carries no mark of its
own, so it has three lines of its own rather than five:

  .claude/skills/ticket-runner/SKILL.md: written
  .claude/skills/ticket-runner/SKILL.md: overwritten, because the copy here said something else
  .claude/skills/ticket-runner/SKILL.md: left alone, because 0.5.0 set this Target up and this is 0.4.0 — upgrade `ticket-runner` to rewrite it

A copy with no number to stamp — a pipeline that could not read its own package
— writes no marker at all, so the document it writes is the document it next
compares against.

`GitHub:` says which labels were created, or that every one of them was already
there, that squash merging is on, and whether deleting a pull request's branch
when it merges was switched on now or found on already:

  branches: switched on deleting a pull request's branch when it merges
  branches: a pull request's branch is already deleted when it merges

A cloud Host can delete nothing on the remote, so that setting is the only way a
merged Ticket's branch goes there, and Target readiness refuses a repository
without it (ADR-0008). Where GitHub could not be asked at all, its one line
says why, and a `gh` that cannot be run is told apart from one that is not
logged in:

  nothing done: `gh` is not authenticated
  nothing done: `gh` is not installed

`Checked:` is one line per item only the human can put right, each marked `✓` or
`✗`, in a fixed order: `gh`, `claude`, the plugin, a CI workflow, a Check.

The `gh` line has two ways to fail, the same two, and only a `gh` that runs is
sent to log in:

  ✗ `gh` is not authenticated — run `gh auth login`
  ✗ `gh` is not installed — install the GitHub CLI from https://cli.github.com

The last line is the exit code in words: `Ready: everything a Run expects of
this Target is in place.` for 0, and `Not ready: <n> items are yours to put
right.` for 1.
